findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews overdue notice counts on the first of every month... The finance office reviews self-checkout usage at the end of each quarter."
findings.fix: Remove this section, or replace it with circulation/revenue data that actually bears on the decision to end fines.
findings.violation: These administrative scheduling details are irrelevant to the pilot results or the fines recommendation and serve no argumentative purpose in the document.

findings.evidence: "dropped from 22 percent of respondents before the pilot to 5 percent after it... The survey was administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot."
findings.fix: Correct the description to say the second survey was taken at the 12-month mark (not "after" the pilot), or explain why a mid-pilot reading stands in for the post-pilot result.
findings.violation: The text labels the second measurement as "after" the pilot, but the pilot lasted 18 months and the survey was taken at month 12, so it was not actually taken after the pilot ended.

findings.evidence: "replacing the current fine notices with automatic email reminders sent three, seven, and fourteen days after the due date"
findings.fix: Either flag the reminder schedule as a separate, untested design choice, or provide evidence/rationale for that specific cadence.
findings.violation: This specific reminder schedule was never part of what was tested in the pilot (which compared fines vs. no fines), so it is being recommended without supporting evidence.

findings.evidence: "matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established"
findings.fix: Present the actual pilot data on return timing that justifies the 60-day cutoff, or remove the claim that it matches an established pattern.
findings.violation: No 60-day return window or any time-bucketed return data was mentioned anywhere in "What the Pilot Showed"; the claim invokes pilot support that was never presented.

findings.evidence: "the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches"
findings.fix: Acknowledge that only half the branches were tested and justify why the result should generalize to the rest, or scope the recommendation more cautiously.
findings.violation: The pilot tested only 5 of the 10 branches; extending the result to all ten branches (including the ones that served as the comparison group) is an unacknowledged generalization beyond the data.

findings.evidence: "The systems team plans to update the online catalog's fine-display field during the same rollout window."
